scope: Security/access reconciliation against shared main working tree; root records final source/commit identity.

claims.conclusion: Unix-socket request classification is per request; public traffic never enters owner API/WebSocket handlers. Socket owner and root are trusted, not isolated adversaries.

Funnel port 443 remains configured while Reach runs. Unknown HTTP requests are gated; closed invitation window does not imply a closed TCP port. Known agent keys, connector addresses and expiring person door keys have separate bounded admission.
Reach removes only its recorded route and a lease janitor attempts cleanup. A five-second lease is not a guarantee of instant cleanup during daemon/network failure.
claims.limits: Live authenticated tailnet/Funnel cleanup still needs acceptance.

claims.conclusion: P-256 signature, audience, key binding, nonce replay, expiry and fixed route allowlists precede scoped dispatch.
Full control intentionally has OS-account authority, including filesystem root, private data, Reach and security UI; no command deny list or shell sandbox. It cannot be promised harmless.

Current owner forms explicitly request fullControlVersion 1. Missing/old/future/wrong-type requests fail with reload guidance. Unversioned stored grants fail before filesystem expansion, expire in owner lists, cannot edit/reopen/renew and cannot open a public invitation window. New invitation and connection approval are required.
Apps-to-Full now requires a new invitation, matching the documented step-up requirement. Existing narrower-to-Apps/Full checks remain.
Owner UI no longer claims legacy hidden-app selections constrain unrestricted Full control; Read only still reports its exclusions.

Preset scopes and route allowlists are derived on each authorized request. Narrow presets retain file exclusions, native protected-window checks and no-link/sandbox helper. Selecting a terminal/IDE under Apps still gives OS-user command capability.
claims.limits: Native window/input checks are not transactional; hostile local OS-user processes are outside isolation.

claims.conclusion: Only the current credential may exchange. Retired credential plus signing key cannot displace a legitimate pending successor. Ordinary in-flight requests retain two-minute overlap; a lost exchange response can retry until the successor is first used.
claims.limits: A cloned agent folder includes the signing key; overlap is not protection against a trusted-runtime compromise.

claims.conclusion: PKCE S256, connection address binding, current-only refresh exchange and confidential client authentication apply. Hosted bearer tokens are a separate explicit trust boundary from signed gateway keys.
claims.limits: Signed-in Claude/Gemini and live claude.ai/ChatGPT connector calls remain acceptance work.

claims.conclusion: Advertised protocols remain 2024-11-05, 2025-03-26 and 2025-06-18. Newer clients negotiate down; unsupported post-initialize protocol headers fail. No claim of full 2025-11-25 or 2026-07-28 support, issuer-response compatibility or signed-in ChatGPT acceptance.
claims.limits: Protocol adoption requires a separate official-spec and live-client compatibility pass.

claims.conclusion: Credential-store identity/nanosecond metadata plus successful-write generation invalidate all four public-door caches; unreadable stores fail closed.

Invited, waiting or connected Apps/Full bind supervision to the approving native Tailscale device. Pausing agent input does not lift this guard. The person-facing message now says access must end; invalidated legacy Full no longer holds the guard.
Same-device identity/name grouping affects presentation only. Another browser needs local approval, Face ID or a verified linked-computer ticket.
Preset API permits 60 seconds to 24 hours; public join window is at most 15 minutes. UI duration choices start at 15 minutes. A shorter valid invitation is not an access widening.

serve --help stdout and stderr must contain Unix-socket support. Failure denies startup with upgrade guidance and never enables an insecure TCP fallback. This capability probe can false-negative if help wording changes.
claims.limits: Real daemon/service variants still need their own platform acceptance.

claims.conclusion: New Reach chats explicitly choose Auto. Resumed chats with no saved mode omit the flag and retain provider settings; an explicit unknown mode falls back to Manual. The comment now distinguishes these cases.
claims.limits: Real signed-in provider behavior is not established by fake-process tests.

claims.conclusion: Challenge, exact origin, RP ID, signature, presence/verification, user handle and counter are checked; user verification is required. Public challenges have a separate bounded pool.
claims.limits: Software authenticator and recorded vectors are not physical Face ID acceptance or independent cryptographic audit.

claims.conclusion: Public passkey sign-in returns a one-use ticket and tagged enrollment key; private redemption binds owner credential to the enrolled node. Removal revokes local credential access; device deletion is asynchronous.
claims.limits: Live OAuth/Tailscale enrollment, phone biometrics and policy isolation remain manual gates.

claims.conclusion: Approval challenges bind request and owner credential; enabling is owner-only, disabling requires its own assertion, denying never needs biometrics.
Five-minute receipts bind claimant secret and Tailscale identity; interrupted issuance fails closed, retry returns one token, revoked token is not reissued.
Mutual links and one-use device-bound tickets authorize cross-computer admission. Device identity alone does not approve; exact linked origins and verified revocation callbacks remain required.
Initial guest section claiming no terminal/AI/screen control is historical. Detailed guest grants can explicitly include these capabilities; guests cannot manage access.
Named profiles intersect stored and current roots/scopes; missing/invalid profiles deny. Shell-capable profiles are not OS filesystem sandboxes.

claims.section: Native screen, input, selection and shortcuts
claims.conclusion: Documented limits and native evidence are from synthetic helpers/toy apps and earlier saved runs, not a model reasoning in a real signed-in application. Owner control leases, pause/revoke and native permission checks remain required.
claims.limits: Physical phone, ordinary overlapping windows and OS failure/suspension remain acceptance gaps.

claims.conclusion: Unrestricted Full shell runs as owner with clean environment, time/output/concurrency bounds and audit records; spawn failure is 503. Revocation cancels monitored process groups but cannot undo effects or contain detached processes.

Narrow file tools use no-symlink descriptor traversal plus kernel sandbox; shared writer coordination serializes overlapping roots and checks live authorization. Files preset edits are immediate without per-action approval.
claims.limits: Completed mutations cannot be undone by revocation.

claims.conclusion: Browser node state and Reach credentials remain in browser storage. XSS, browser extension or browser-profile compromise are inside this trust boundary. App and browser nodes need separate approval.
claims.limits: Real networks, Tailscale login and physical mobile storage eviction remain acceptance work.

claims.conclusion: Preferences and pauses filter delivery; notification contents/navigation have separate validation. No new claim of real push delivery is made.
claims.limits: Physical push delivery is unverified in this reconciliation.

claims.conclusion: Agent runtime hashes are verified and owner-controlled updates pin an exact package version. Agent runtime auto-update trusts the invited host; this is deliberate remote-code trust and can be disabled.
claims.limits: Live published update recovery and signed-in agent reconnection need release acceptance.

claims.conclusion: Older severity tables, counts, recorded live-tailnet observations and restart statements document earlier passes. They are not assertions that every current line, platform or physical device was exercised.
claims.limits: Current release evidence must be tied to the final commit/source digest by the parent validation task.

claims.section: DoS, supply chain and trust limits
claims.conclusion: Bounded requests, pools and rate limits reduce abuse but do not certify public-service resilience. OS-user access, public custom passkey verifier, detached effects, disk/resource exhaustion, dependency/runtime trust and independent review remain material limits.
